title: Kalinga
capsule: Kalinga was an ancient kingdom occupying the coastal region of present-day Odisha and northern Andhra Pradesh, attested as a powerful independent polity from at least the fourth century BCE. It was conquered by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in c. 261 BCE in a war that by his own Edicts left 100,000 dead and 150,000 deported; the moral revulsion Ashoka expressed at this destruction is credited as the catalyst for his conversion to Buddhism and the propagation of dhamma. Kalinga recovered independence following the Mauryan collapse and remained a significant maritime power, with the Mahameghavahana dynasty ruling in the second–first centuries BCE, before being absorbed into successive empires over the following centuries.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The coastal Odisha core of Kalinga is well-attested by Ashokan Rock Edicts and Mahameghavahana inscriptions, but the boundaries of the independent pre-Mauryan kingdom and its post-Mauryan successors are imprecisely known.
